Run ESLint with --fix to auto-convert." * cannotAutoFix: "Cannot auto-fix: {{reason}}. Manual migration to @implements required." * multiStoryDetected: "Multiple @story annotations detected in the same comment block. Manually convert to separate @implements lines." - create() visitor: - On Program, gets all comments, filters to Block comments, and runs processComment() on each, enforcing the above behavior.

traceability.notes:
The story 010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-IMPLEMENTS is fully implemented.
Mapping to acceptance criteria and REQs: - Optional Warning & Configurable Enforcement (REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING, REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY): The rule `prefer-implements-annotation` is implemented as a suggestion-type ESLint rule that is disabled by default (not present in recommended/strict configs). It can be turned on with severities "off"/"warn"/"error" via standard ESLint configuration, and tests explicitly verify both the default-off behavior and custom severities. - Auto-fix Support & Single Story Conversion (REQ-AUTO-FIX, REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX): The rule declares `fixable: "code"` and provides auto-fix logic which converts simple legacy `@story` + `@req` blocks into a single `@implements` line. Tests confirm both the single requirement case and the multiple-requirement case (all REQ IDs concatenated into a single @implements line). - Multi-story Detection and Non-fixable Scenarios (REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT): The implementation detects and reports mixed `@story`/`@req`/`@implements` usage with `cannotAutoFix` plus a reason, and detects multiple @story paths with `multiStoryDetected`. Tests assert both messages occur under the correct conditions and that no auto-fix is produced for these cases. - Preserve Order and JSDoc Structure (REQ-PRESERVE-FORMAT): The fixer replaces only the lines containing @story and @req, using the original line prefix (indentation and `*`) for the new @implements line and leaving all other content (description, @param, @returns, etc.) unchanged. This maintains the comment’s structure and ordering as described in the story. - Both Formats Valid & Backward Compatibility (REQ-BACKWARD-COMP-VALIDATION, acceptance criterion "Both Formats Valid"): Valid cases explicitly show that comments containing only @story, only @req, or only @implements are ignored by this rule. Combined with the rule being off by default and separate validation rules for annotation syntax/semantics, this ensures legacy formats remain valid regardless of this rule’s configuration. - Quality Standards & Valid Output (REQ-VALID-OUTPUT): The auto-fix activates only for unambiguous, single-story patterns with simple `@story ` and `@req ` lines. For complex @story or @req content, tests verify that diagnostics are still reported but no fix is applied, preventing invalid or ambiguous output. Other rules’ tests confirm that the generated @implements syntax is accepted by format and deep-reference validators. - Documentation (migration guide and examples): docs/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.md documents how to enable and use this rule, includes before/after auto-fix examples that match the story, and provides configuration guidance for off/warn/error. This satisfies the documentation acceptance criterion.
Given the dedicated rule, comprehensive tests tied to this story, working plugin integration, and consistent documentation, all acceptance criteria and technical requirements for this story are met.
